key_findings.finding: The retrieved ORD records directly support the same transformation with the same alkyl chloride core: 3-chloropropyl oxazolidinone reacts with piperazine-substituted azaheteroarenes to give 3-(piperazin-1-yl)propyl products. The matched examples include pyridyl and diazine/triazine-like heteroaromatic amines, supporting chemoselective alkylation at the free secondary piperazine N rather than ring nitrogens or the exocyclic heteroaromatic amino site.

key_findings.finding: Reported conditions in the matched records are consistent with base-promoted SN2: potassium carbonate or carbonate salts, often iodide (likely Finkelstein activation/catalytic iodide), with 1-butanol listed as solvent/additive; some records include HCl salts and inorganic counterions. key_findings.finding: The alkyl chloride is a primary 3-chloropropyl electrophile and is the key leaving-group-bearing component; the heteroaromatic amine functions mainly as a piperazine nucleophile bearing an electron-poor azaaryl substituent.
